definitions.explanation: A series of successive defeats without any wins in between. Used in sports, games, competitions, and other contests.

examples.japanese: ⟦チーム→チーム：03858_chiimu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{今|いま}→今：00945_ima⟧、5{連敗|れんぱい}⟦{中|ちゅう}→〜中：09840_chuu⟧⟦だ→だ：09496_da⟧。
examples.english: The team is currently on a 5-game losing streak.

examples.japanese: {連敗|れんぱい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{止|と}めたい→止める：00678_tomeru⟧。
examples.english: I want to stop the losing streak.

examples.japanese: {連敗|れんぱい}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{続|つづ}いて→続く：00903_tsuzuku⟧⟦チーム→チーム：03858_chiimu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{士気|しき}→士気：19824_shiki⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{下|さ}がっている→下がる：01188_sagaru⟧。
examples.english: The continuous losses have lowered the team's morale.

examples.japanese: ⟦やっと→やっと：01561_yatto⟧{連敗|れんぱい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{脱出|だっしゅつ}して→脱出：13934_dasshutsu⟧⟦{一勝|いっしょう}→一勝：29129_isshou⟧⟦できた→できる：00557_dekiru⟧。
examples.english: We finally broke out of the losing streak and got a win.

examples.japanese: 10{連敗|れんぱい}⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦したら→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{監督|かんとく}→監督：00185_kantoku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{責任|せきにん}→責任：03298_sekinin⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{問|と}われる→問う：02299_tou⟧⟦だろう→だろう：09576_darou⟧。
examples.english: If they lose 10 in a row, the manager will surely be held accountable.

notes:
{連敗|れんぱい} is a run of consecutive defeats, most often in sports reporting but also in elections, court cases, and any repeated contest. A number attaches directly with no counter in between: 3{連敗|れんぱい} (three straight losses), 10{連敗|れんぱい} (ten straight losses).

COMMON PATTERNS:
- As a ⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧-verb it takes no object — the loser is the subject: ⟦チーム→チーム：03858_chiimu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧3{連敗|れんぱい}⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧.
- N{連敗|れんぱい}⟦{中|ちゅう}→〜中：09840_chuu⟧: the streak is still running.
- {連敗|れんぱい}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{続|つづ}く→続く：00903_tsuzuku⟧: the losses go on.
- {連敗|れんぱい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{止|と}める→止める：00678_tomeru⟧ / {連敗|れんぱい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{脱出|だっしゅつ}→脱出：13934_dasshutsu⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: break the streak.
- {連敗|れんぱい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{喫|きっ}する→喫する：29124_kissuru⟧: suffer consecutive losses (formal, newspaper style).

The streak counts only losses, so a single ⟦{一勝|いっしょう}→一勝：29129_isshou⟧ ends it — which is why the two words so often appear in the same sentence.

WORD FORMATION: {連|れん} (consecutive) + {敗|はい} (defeat). The same {連|れん} gives ⟦{連勝|れんしょう}→連勝：06528_renshou⟧ and ⟦{連続|れんぞく}→連続：03783_renzoku⟧.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{連勝|れんしょう}→連勝：06528_renshou⟧ is the antonym and behaves identically, except that a winning streak normally ⟦{止|と}まる→止まる：00555_tomaru⟧ (intransitive) while a losing streak is something you ⟦{止|と}める→止める：00678_tomeru⟧.
- ⟦{連続|れんぞく}→連続：03783_renzoku⟧⟦{敗北|はいぼく}→敗北：12872_haiboku⟧ is the formal, non-sporting way to say the same thing.
- ⟦スランプ→スランプ：29125_suranpu⟧ and ⟦{低迷|ていめい}→低迷：09332_teimei⟧ describe the poor form behind a streak rather than the losses themselves.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {連敗|れんぱい}⟦{脱出|だっしゅつ}→脱出：13934_dasshutsu⟧: breaking out of a losing streak (headline style)
- ⟦{泥沼|どろぬま}→泥沼：11065_doronuma⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{連敗|れんぱい}: a quagmire of consecutive losses
- {連敗|れんぱい}⟦{地獄|じごく}→地獄：12053_jigoku⟧: losing-streak hell (informal)
